subject: Immediate: Live SDK header inconsistency causing checkout slowdowns
messages:
From: Maya Patel (FastCommerce) <maya.patel@fastcommerce.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: FastCommerce SRE Team <sre@fastcommerce.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent checkout slowdowns — suspect SDK integration

Hi Tessa —

We started seeing a burst of errors and p99 latency spikes on our checkout pipeline around 08:45 PT. Error rate for POST /v1/live/generate jumped from ~0.2% to ~6% and throughput dropped by ~35%. Our SREs captured a pcap and a short log excerpt (attached).

Symptoms we observed:
- Repeated "header parse failed" entries in the connector logs (examples in attached log).
- Partial responses from the Redwood live endpoint (stream truncated) followed by client retries.
- Spikes correlate with checkout flash events but the same SDK versions were in use earlier without issue.

We haven't changed our client-side batching logic; we're on the official JS SDK v2.3.1. Can your team confirm whether there are known reassembly problems with the streaming parser or a regression? This is impacting customers. We need an initial triage and ETA for a mitigation.

Attachments: fastcommerce-checkout-logs-20270629.log, ingest-pcap-20270629.pcap

Thanks,
Maya Patel
Head of Platform Ops — FastCommerce

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Maya Patel (FastCommerce) <maya.patel@fastcommerce.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent checkout slowdowns — suspect SDK integration

Hi all — initial triage results (summary):

What I saw:
- The pcap shows frequent small frame boundaries where a single logical header block is split across multiple TCP segments. Our streaming parser expects headers to be coalesced before parse; in stressed paths the dechunker sometimes emits a partial header token into the parser.
- When that happens the parser returns a recoverable error but the client-side SDK treats it as terminal and retries, which amplifies load. We also observed KV-cache invalidation events causing extra cold-path latency.

Likely root cause:
- A race in the ingest reassembly pipeline: under high fan-in the dechunker will forward partial header tokens when the underlying socket buffer hits a threshold. Combined with a recent change to stricter header validation (rolled in last month) this converts recoverable partials into hard parse failures.

Immediate mitigation (recommended):
1) Toggle the lenient-reassembly flag on the FastCommerce ingest gateway (server-side config) — this causes the dechunker to buffer until a complete header sequence is seen.
2) As a short-term client mitigation, increase SDK per-connection receive buffer and add 200ms jitter to retries to avoid retry storms.

Planned fix:
- We'll land a targeted runtime patch that: 1) makes the parser tolerant to split header tokens, and 2) avoids generating client-visible terminal errors for partial token cases. I estimate a patch + canary deploy in the dedicated ingest fleet within 24–36 hours (if approved).

Attachments: parser-trace.txt (short trace showing the split-token path).

Karthik Iyer
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference
From: FastCommerce SRE Team <sre@fastcommerce.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 13:20:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent checkout slowdowns — suspect SDK integration

Karthik / team — thanks for the quick analysis. We applied the lenient-reassembly toggle at 12:10 PT and saw error rate drop from ~6% to ~0.9% and p99 latency improve by ~40%. Throughput is still ~20% below normal during peak events, likely due to the accumulated retry storm and some lingering KV-cache misses.

We've attached the requested pcap (ingest-pcap-20270629.pcap) and the post-toggle metrics. Can you confirm:
- ETA for the runtime patch with canary?
- Any recommended rollback plan if the canary has unintended perf regressions?

Also, leadership at FastCommerce is asking for a short exec readout and any proposed customer credits for the incident window.

— FastCommerce SRE
